chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them) both said: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar both said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi, on the authority of Marwan ibn Muslim that Ibn Abu al-Awja' entered the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

and said: 'Do you not claim that Allah is the Creator of Everything?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied, 'Most certainly.' He said: 'I also create.' The Imam (peace be upon him) asked him, 'How do you create?' He responded, 'I relieve my bowels in a place, then I stay away from it, and it makes insects. Therefore, this is my creation.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied, 'Is not the creator of something aware of what he has created?' He answered, 'Why not?' The Imam (peace be upon him) said: 'So, can you distinguish the male from the female, and the young from the old, among those insects?' The reporter says: Ibn Abu al-Awja' kept silent.

key_terms.أَحْدَثُ: I generate/create (from the root of hadith/emergence)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq refute the claim that humans are true creators?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* illustrates the Shia theological distinction between *khalq* (divine creative agency) and *huduth* (natural emergence or change). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes Ibn Abu al-Awja’s materialist claim by highlighting that true creation requires comprehensive knowledge of the created entity’s attributes, such as gender and lifespan, which mere natural processes lack. This argument underscores the concept of *Ilm al-Ilah* (Divine Knowledge) as an essential attribute of the Creator, distinguishing Him from accidental or partial causes.
